subject.title: Feature: channels.slack.ignoreSubtypes config key to suppress message_changed / message_deleted events

question: Should Slack edit/delete subtype events remain observable system events by default, gain an opt-in `channels.slack.ignoreSubtypes` suppression list, or be handled through a different existing Slack policy surface?
rationale: The source behavior is clear, but accepting a new public channel config key and deciding which Slack system events may be dropped is a maintainer product/config contract choice.

options.title: Add opt-in ignoreSubtypes
options.body: Allow teams to suppress specific Slack subtype system events while preserving current default behavior for upgrades.

options.title: Keep current system events
options.body: Leave edit/delete events visible to sessions and document agent or prompt policy as the supported workaround.

options.title: Choose a narrower built-in policy
options.body: Drop only edit/delete events by default or through an existing Slack policy surface without adding a generic subtype list.

recommendation.title: Add opt-in ignoreSubtypes
recommendation.body: Allow teams to suppress specific Slack subtype system events while preserving current default behavior for upgrades.

likelyOwner.reason: The current edit/delete subtype system-event behavior appears to date to steipete's gating commit, making him the clearest available routing owner for the policy choice.
